bibleSpine.kjv: He that is unjust, let him be unjust still: and he which is filthy, let him be filthy still: and he that is righteous, let him be righteous still: and he that is holy, let him be holy still.
bibleSpine.gloss: The decree that fixes every character forever — the precise moment probation closes. No one changes sides after this word; each is sealed in what he has become. It is spoken because intercession is about to end.

bibleSpine.kjv: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.
bibleSpine.gloss: The close of probation runs straight into the second coming: the fixing of character (v.11) and the rewarding advent (v.12) are one connected event. 'I come quickly' is why the door of mercy shuts first.

bibleSpine.kjv: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God, and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple, till the seven plagues of the seven angels were fulfilled.
bibleSpine.gloss: The heavenly sanctuary is closed by God's own glory: no priest, no ministration, no intercession while the plagues fall. This is the throne-room picture of Christ having ceased to plead — the saints now live under a holy God with the temple shut.

bibleSpine.kjv: And I heard a great voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.
bibleSpine.gloss: The plagues begin the instant the temple is closed (15:8 → 16:1): the wrath poured out is 'unmingled with mercy' precisely because the Mediator no longer stands between God and man.

bibleSpine.kjv: And there shall be no man in the tabernacle of the congregation when he goeth in to make an atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made an atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the congregation of Israel.
bibleSpine.gloss: The type of the closed temple: on the Day of Atonement no one might be in the sanctuary while the high priest finished the atonement. The antitype is Rev. 15:8 — while Christ completes the final atonement, no man can enter; when He comes out, probation is closed.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days; then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.
bibleSpine.gloss: The cleansing of the sanctuary is the final phase of Christ's priestly work — the investigative judgment that decides every case before He ceases to intercede. When it ends, the temple is shut (Rev. 15:8) and probation closes (Rev. 22:11).

bibleSpine.kjv: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
bibleSpine.gloss: Michael (Christ) 'stands up' — rises from His mediatorial seat, His priestly work finished. The instant He ceases to intercede, the unequalled time of trouble breaks; yet 'thy people shall be delivered,' every one written in the book — saved out of the very crisis.

bibleSpine.kjv: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
bibleSpine.gloss: Before Michael stands up, a people is 'purified, and made white, and tried' — the victory work that must be finished while the Advocate still pleads. The filthy stay filthy, the holy stay holy (Rev. 22:11); character is now permanent.

bibleSpine.kjv: Ask ye now, and see whether a man doth travail with child? wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?
bibleSpine.gloss: The anguish of the time of Jacob's trouble — pangs like a woman in travail, every face pale. This is the saints' distress after mercy's door has shut, without an intercessor to plead their case.

bibleSpine.kjv: Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.
bibleSpine.gloss: The name text: 'the time of Jacob's trouble' — a day like no other, matching Daniel's 'such as never was.' The promise seals it: 'but he shall be saved out of it.' The saints are not saved FROM the trouble but delivered THROUGH it.

bibleSpine.kjv: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.
bibleSpine.gloss: The historical type. Jacob, alone in the night, expecting Esau's sword, wrestles with the Angel — a picture of the sealed saint pleading alone in the final crisis, his salvation seemingly hanging on a single night of importunity.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.
bibleSpine.gloss: 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me' — the language of the saints in the time of Jacob's trouble. They cling in agony to a God whose face seems hidden, and prevail not by their merit but by holding fast to His covenant.

bibleSpine.kjv: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.
bibleSpine.gloss: The supplanter becomes the prince who prevails. His victory is granted only because his sin was already confessed and forgiven before that night — the type of saints whose sins have gone beforehand to judgment, so nothing remains to condemn them.

bibleSpine.kjv: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Bethel, and there he spake with us;
bibleSpine.gloss: The inspired commentary on Jacob's wrestling: he 'prevailed' by weeping and supplication, not force. So the saints overcome the final crisis by tears and clinging prayer — the wrestling of a heart that will not let God go.

bibleSpine.kjv: Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.
bibleSpine.gloss: Before probation closes, the servants of God are sealed in their foreheads — settled into the truth so they cannot be moved. The sealing must be finished (7:3) before Christ ceases interceding (Rev. 15:8); the sealed alone stand without a mediator.

bibleSpine.kjv: Slay utterly old and young, both maids, and little children, and women: but come not near any man upon whom is the mark: and begin at my sanctuary. Then they began at the ancient men which were before the house.
bibleSpine.gloss: The type of the sealing before the slaughter: the destroyer may not touch any who bear the mark. Judgment begins at the house of God (cf. 1 Pet. 4:17). Only the sealed are sheltered when the plagues fall and no Mediator stands between.

bibleSpine.kjv: But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth? for he is like a refiner's fire, and like fullers' soap:
bibleSpine.gloss: The question the whole crisis answers: who shall stand when He appears? Only those refined and purified BEFORE the day — cleansed by the blood while the Advocate still pleads, so they can stand in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor.

bibleSpine.kjv: He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
bibleSpine.gloss: Christ's confession of the overcomer's name before the Father is His intercessory act. It is finished for each case in the investigative judgment; those whose names remain unblotted are ready to face the trouble with every case already decided for life.

symbolDefs.symbol: the close of probation (intercession ended; every case decided)
symbolDefs.meaning: The moment Christ's priestly mediation ends and each character is fixed forever. Scripture defines it by its own words: the decree 'let him be unjust still... let him be holy still' (Rev. 22:11) is spoken because 'I come quickly' (Rev. 22:12); the heavenly temple is then 'filled with smoke... and no man was able to enter' (Rev. 15:8) — no ministration, as in the type when 'there shall be no man in the tabernacle' while the high priest made atonement (Lev. 16:17); Michael 'stands up,' His work as intercessor finished (Dan. 12:1). Every case has been decided in the cleansing of the sanctuary (Dan. 8:14) — the investigative judgment — so the sealed 'shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book' (Dan. 12:1). The saints then live in the sight of a holy God with no advocate to plead sin, having ceased from sin while the Advocate still pleaded (Dan. 12:10; Mal. 3:2).

symbolDefs.symbol: the time of Jacob's trouble (the sealed saints' anguish without an intercessor, yet saved)
symbolDefs.meaning: The unequalled final crisis of the righteous after probation closes: 'a time of trouble, such as never was' (Dan. 12:1) is 'even the time of Jacob's trouble; but he shall be saved out of it' (Jer. 30:7). The type is Jacob left alone at night, wrestling the Angel with 'I will not let thee go, except thou bless me' (Gen. 32:24, 26), prevailing by weeping and supplication (Hos. 12:4) to become 'Israel... a prince' who 'hast prevailed' (Gen. 32:28). The saints, sealed in their foreheads (Rev. 7:3) and marked so the destroyer cannot touch them (Ezek. 9:6), endure travail-pangs and pale faces (Jer. 30:6) while God's face seems hidden — yet they cling to the covenant because their sins have already gone to judgment and been blotted out. They are not spared the trouble but 'delivered' and 'saved out of it,' every name unblotted from the book of life (Dan. 12:1; Rev. 3:5).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Those who are living upon the earth when the intercession of Christ shall cease in the sanctuary above are to stand in the sight of a holy God without a mediator. Their robes must be spotless, their characters must be purified from sin by the blood of sprinkling.
witnesses.gloss: The section's thesis in her own words: after intercession ceases the saints stand 'without a mediator,' which is why the purifying work must be finished beforehand — 'through the grace of God and their own diligent effort.'

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Then Jesus ceases His intercession in the sanctuary above. He lifts His hands and with a loud voice says, 'It is done;'... 'He that is unjust, let him be unjust still... and he that is holy, let him be holy still.' Revelation 22:11. Every case has been decided for life or death. Christ has made the atonement for His people and blotted out their sins.
witnesses.gloss: Ties Rev. 22:11 directly to the ceasing of intercession and 'every case... decided' — the exact link between the close-of-probation decree and the end of mediation the section owns.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When He leaves the sanctuary, darkness covers the inhabitants of the earth. In that fearful time the righteous must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor.
witnesses.gloss: States the section's key phrase — the righteous 'must live in the sight of a holy God without an intercessor' — locating it precisely when Christ leaves the sanctuary (Rev. 15:8).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: When the work of the investigative judgment closes, the destiny of all will have been decided for life or death. Probation is ended a short time before the appearing of the Lord in the clouds of heaven. Christ in the Revelation... declares: 'He that is unjust, let him be unjust still... Revelation 22:11, 12.'
witnesses.gloss: Confirms the investigative judgment (Dan. 8:14) as the deciding of 'the destiny of all,' ended by the Rev. 22:11-12 decree — the sanctuary-cleansing and close-of-probation chain the spine builds.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: But there will be no time then to do it and no Mediator to plead their cause before the Father. Before this time the awfully solemn declaration has gone forth, 'He that is unjust, let him be unjust still... and he that is holy, let him be holy still.'
witnesses.gloss: Explicitly names 'no Mediator to plead their cause' as following the Rev. 22:11 declaration — corroborating that the victory over 'every besetment' must precede the crisis (the source cites EW 71).

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: They lay hold of the strength of God as Jacob laid hold of the Angel; and the language of their souls is: 'I will not let Thee go, except Thou bless me.'
witnesses.gloss: Draws the Genesis 32:26 type straight onto the saints in the time of trouble — clinging to God through the anguish exactly as Jacob wrestled the Angel.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: So, in the time of trouble, if the people of God had unconfessed sins to appear before them while tortured with fear and anguish, they would be overwhelmed... But while they have a deep sense of their unworthiness, they have no concealed wrongs to reveal. Their sins have gone beforehand to judgment and have been blotted out.
witnesses.gloss: The 'sins gone beforehand to judgment' text the section calls for — explaining why the saints can endure the trouble without a mediator: nothing remains on the books to condemn them.

witnesses.author: Ellen G. White
witnesses.quote: Christ is waiting with longing desire for the manifestation of Himself in His church. When the character of Christ shall be perfectly reproduced in His people, then He will come to claim them as His own.
witnesses.gloss: Grounds why the victory message must precede the crisis: the character-perfecting must be finished while the Advocate pleads, so the saints can stand when probation closes.

witnesses.author: Uriah Smith
witnesses.quote: the temple is filled with smoke from the glory of God, and no being can enter into the temple, or sanctuary, till they have fulfilled their work; there will therefore be no ministration in the sanctuary during this time... for Christ is then no longer a mediator; mercy, which has long stayed the hand of vengeance, pleads no more; the servants of God are all sealed.
witnesses.gloss: Pioneer exposition of Rev. 15:8 (Daniel and the Revelation): the closed, smoke-filled temple means 'Christ is then no longer a mediator' and 'the servants of God are all sealed' — independent corroboration of the section's core reading.

witnesses.author: William Miller
witnesses.quote: 'And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great Prince which standeth for the children of thy people.' Michael, in this passage, must mean Christ; he is the great Prince, and Prince of princes.
witnesses.gloss: The earliest pioneer voice identifying Michael of Daniel 12:1 as Christ — the priestly Prince who 'stands up' — anchoring the sanctuary/close-of-probation reading in Miller's own exposition.

historyAnchor: The doctrine took its settled shape among the Millerite Adventists after 1844, when the sanctuary-cleansing of Daniel 8:14 was understood as Christ's final atoning ministry preceding the close of probation.
uncertainties: EW 71 is a single printed page; the verified quotations above come from paragraphs EW 71.1 and EW 71.2. The section's own 'reflect the image of Jesus fully' language sits in EW 71.1 and the 'no Mediator... he that is unjust' language in EW 71.2 — cite by paragraph, not the bare page, for precision.

On the nature of Christ: this section does not itself argue the nature-of-Christ point, but its logic (the saints 'have ceased from sin while the Advocate still pleads') rests on the prior sections' honest resolution — He took fallen, weakened humanity yet never consented to sin; statements guarding His sinlessness are about consent and character, not an unfallen nature. Keep that framing consistent when this section is read alongside the nature-of-Christ sections.

GC 490.2 falls in the earlier 'Investigative Judgment' chapter (p. 490) rather than the 'Time of Trouble' chapter (pp. 613ff); it is cited here for the close-of-probation/every-case-decided link, which it states verbatim, not as a time-of-trouble passage.
